C01.title: The study door
C01.summary: Bolted on the inside, the Master's own key in the lock, the bolt-plate splintered where it was forced.

C02.title: The windows
C02.summary: Every sash felted, shutters barred, hearth damper shut. The room was sealed against draughts.

C03.title: The wall lamp bracket
C03.summary: Collar crooked, the joint beneath a half-turn loose, yellow wax under the rim and a hardened drip below.

C04.title: The lamp valve
C04.summary: Burner tap wide open, a thin brass shim wedged in the valve's thermal strip.

C05.title: The toast draft
C05.summary: A toast announcing retirement, the sale to the Osterhal League, Corvane dropped, and a public 'forgiveness' of the foreman of Cinder Row.

C06.title: The desk drawer
C06.summary: A private-inquiry report: Lady Cordelia and Dr. Quillon meet weekly. The Master's margin: 'Confront after the gala.'

C07.title: The French window
C07.summary: The latch lifts from outside; lamp-black on the frame; a torn maid's cuff stamped Corby's Agency.

C08.title: Ledger page (safe)
C08.summary: 3,000 crowns paid to G. Loam: 'Inquiry matter, 1166.'

C09.title: Mantle drawings (safe)
C09.summary: Mantle drawings signed E. Marrow, 1181, marked by the Master 'File as Works patent.'

C10.title: The sale contract (safe)
C10.summary: Sale to the Osterhal League, signed by Stenn, awaiting the Master at midnight. Corvane's consultancy is struck through.

C11.title: The hired-staff list
C11.summary: An extra maid, 'Ida March', engaged on Miss Odalys's order; she left before collecting her wages.

C12.title: Hob's account
C12.summary: Odalys and the Master quarrelled at ten to nine. He bolted himself in at 9:02 and had a light by 9:05.

C13.title: The missed toast, and the door
C13.summary: Toast due 10:30; Pell announced a delay at 10:32; Corvane stood in; the door was forced at 11:40.

C14.title: Corvane on the terrace
C14.summary: Corvane left with Halvard Stenn at 9:45 and was back by 10:05.

C15.title: Ned's account
C15.summary: Only one maid used the French window all day (6:35 to 6:50). Quillon and Cordelia were under the palms 9:35 to 10:05.

C16.title: The key register
C16.summary: Spare study key out 4:50 PM, in 5:25 PM, signed T.P. It is the only entry that day.

C17.title: Household statements
C17.summary: Collar clean at 7:30 AM; the study is always locked; a lamp trim takes 10 to 15 minutes; Corvane never left the library from 6 to 7.

C18.title: The cabinet wax
C18.summary: A lavender beeswax cake, one corner freshly cut since four o'clock.

C19.title: The cook's account
C19.summary: Pell was in the kitchen from 9:15, save a quarter-hour near 10:25. The cook never left her range.

C20.title: The cellar wrench
C20.summary: A small chain-wrench with wax and brass dust in its jaws; one link of the chain is bent.

C21.title: The old tin
C21.summary: A fitter's tin of OW-6 brass shims, eleven of twelve; each has the same chipped '6'.

C22.title: The small box
C22.summary: Josiah Pell's whistle and Commissioner Loam's confession letter.

C23.title: The gate ledger
C23.summary: Corvane at the Works 6:10 AM to 5:35 PM; Odalys 8:20 AM to 6:10 PM; the Master with Corvane until 5:35.

C24.title: The personnel book
C24.summary: T. Pell, apprentice fitter, 1145 to 1150. J. Pell, foreman, dismissed 1166, died 1169. Next of kin: brother T. Pell.

C25.title: The plaque proof
C25.summary: A proof plaque naming Foreman J. Pell's 'negligence', 'whom the Master forgave'.

C26.title: The bypass page and training roll
C26.summary: The Old Pattern servicing job takes about twenty minutes. Taught to Corvane, E. Marrow, T. Pell and others. OW-6 shims went to apprentices before 1152.

C27.title: The appointment book and the cabs
C27.summary: Cordelia and Quillon at the infirmary 4:30 to 5:50 PM; cab to Marrowgate at 5:52.

C28.title: The demand letter
C28.summary: The Master demanded 1,200 crowns from Quillon by month-end.

C29.title: The medical file
C29.summary: The Master lost his sense of smell in 1181. Household aware. Gas-safe lamps advised, advice not taken.

C30.title: Ilsa's papers
C30.summary: Rejected patent petitions; her father's letters; his fitter's kit sold in 1183; a note from Odalys telling her to come as a maid.

C31.title: The tool roll and pawn ticket
C31.summary: Only smooth-jaw spanners. A chain-wrench pawned on the 17th of Reapmonth, still on Grubb's shelf.

C32.title: Ilsa's account
C32.summary: Ilsa was in the study 6:35 to 6:50 and saw the union already packed with wax.

C33.title: A wire to Vennard House
C33.summary: Loam wired Pell on the 11th of Reapmonth: 'I have wronged your brother.'

C34.title: The clerk's memory
C34.summary: Pell collected the wire in person, read it twice, and left white as chalk.

C35.title: A wire to Corvane
C35.summary: Stenn to Corvane: the Master signs at midnight; his League board seat follows the signature.

C36.title: The inquiry file, 1166
C36.summary: Fourteen dead; an unvented oil store; blame placed on Foreman J. Pell; signed Commissioner Loam.

C37.title: The archivist's account
C37.summary: Loam died on the 13th of Reapmonth; his sealed statement never arrived; the foreman's brother asked for the file every anniversary.

C38.title: The autopsy
C38.summary: Coal-gas poisoning. Unconscious by about half past ten at the latest. No struggle.

C39.title: The lab report
C39.summary: Household wax that softens in about an hour; an old-works OW-6 shim with a chipped die; union scored by the bent-link wrench.

timeline.text: Nell polishes the study lamp's collar. It is straight and clean.
The Master locks the study with his own key and leaves.
The Master signs in at the Lampworks.
The lavender wax cake in the pantry is still whole.
The spare study key is signed out: T.P.
The spare study key is signed back in.
The Master and Mr. Corvane leave the Lampworks together.
Lady Cordelia and Dr. Quillon leave the infirmary in one cab.
Miss Odalys leaves the Lampworks.
A maid slips through the French window into the study.
The maid slips out again.
Odalys and the Master quarrel in the passage outside the study.
The Master bolts himself in. A light shows under the door by five past.
Pell sits down with the cook in the kitchen.
Dr. Quillon and Lady Cordelia stand together under the palms until about five past ten.
Mr. Corvane leaves the ballroom with Halvard Stenn.
Mr. Corvane is back in the ballroom.
By the laboratory's reckoning the wax would begin to run about an hour after the lamp was lit.
Pell knocks at the study door and gets no answer.
The toast is due. By the surgeon's account the Master is already unconscious, at the latest.
Pell tells the hall that the Master begs a little time.
Mr. Corvane gives a stand-in toast.
Pell and Hob force the door. The lamp is out and the room reeks of gas. Pell shuts the supply and opens the shutters.
Dr. Quillon is called and pronounces apoplexy.
'Ida March' leaves without collecting her wages.

official.text: Master Vennard withdrew to his study after dinner, suffered a seizure of apoplexy, and died shortly before he was found at twenty to midnight.
official.challenged: Challenged: the surgeon puts him unconscious by half past ten at the latest, and the laboratory says the lamp was made a trap hours before he died.
